subject: Community Control Over Public Surveillance Ordinance
overview: The committee reviewed and amended a proposed ordinance requiring transparency and City Council oversight for the acquisition and use of surveillance technologies. The body approved several amendments to exempt routine city tools and reported the ordinance to the full Council with a favorable recommendation.

items.title: Presentation of CCOPS Ordinance
items.summary: Councilor Collins provided an overview of the draft Community Control over Public Surveillance (CCOPS) ordinance, detailing modifications made to reporting requirements and technology exemptions.

items.title: Departmental Concerns and Capacity
items.summary: Police Chief Jack Buckley expressed concern regarding the administrative burden of reporting requirements and the potential impact on department capacity.

items.title: Review of Exemptions and Routine Technologies
items.summary: City department heads and administration staff requested clarifications and exemptions for technologies including traffic signal sensors, code enforcement photography, and event broadcasting tools.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Residents and representatives from several local advocacy organizations spoke in support of the ordinance as a tool for building public trust and protecting civil liberties.

items.title: Amendments and Reporting of Paper
items.summary: Approved several amendments to technical definitions and exemptions before voting to report the ordinance to the full City Council as amended.
